title: Quitting Armstrong and calling out the band on intonation
summary: His solos were taken away, so he told the band they played out of tune and Louis backed him.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: What was the incident that caused you to quit Louie? It wasn't the Man With the Funny Horn; was it?
It wasn't exactly The Man With The Funny Horn, but it got so that I couldn't get any solos. They took most of my solos away, and in fact, I was getting pretty popular in there.

I can say that Louie was with me, because I got up in rehearsal one day and this is important because Louie stood up for me--I said, look you fellows, I know I don't come from New Orleans and I'm glad I don't because the way you guys play and the way that I came up with such wonderful musicians, I said if it wasn't for this man--Louie was right there--I said if it wasn't for this man, you guys wouldn't be able to get a job noplace, because you guys play out of tune, and I said that worried me to death,

because that was one of the main things, you never heard a man on any recording playing out of tune. I gave them the devil, and after that Louie called me over and said you gave them hell and I'm sure glad of it.
Louie was funny that way, he didn't want to settle any disputes, so that's why some of those guys wound up getting fired in that band.
